newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX recovers on gains to VSZ share.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX recovers on gains to VSZ share.

text.p: The Slovak SAX index recovered slightly on Tuesday, edging up to 168.00 points from 166.63 in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE), boosted by gains to steel maker VSZ.
VSZ traded 18,132 shares on the main floor, closing up 10 crowns at 655.
"Trading with this traditionally liquid paper (VSZ) revived on Tuesday. However, the closing price was lifted by...a 10,000 share bloc," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said.
Apart from the bloc, which was matched at 655 crowns, VSZ was traded mostly at around 640 to 647 crowns in the continuous session, Sykora said.
Oil refinery Slovnaft, the most heavily-weighted share on the index, added four crowns to close at 865, on 366 shares traded.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta closed up 60 crowns to 1,210, on 7,867 shares.
Brokers have also said they expect the market to become more transparent soon, after the BSE announced it would introduce a new division of its trading markets from August this year.
"If nothing else, this will separate the liquid shares from those which are illiquid, which should encourage some investors to operate on this market again," Sykora added.
Overall, volume fell to 96,165 shares, from 310,609 shares traded on Monday, while turnover decreased to 50.54 million crowns, from 91.55 million.
